Hypothesis: The bug is in `TTLCache.expire` at line 557, which uses `time > curr.expires` as the expiration condition, while `__contains__`, `__getitem__`, `__delitem__`, and `__iter__` all use `not (time < curr.expires)` / `time < curr.expires` (i.e., expiration happens when `time >= expires`, not `time > expires`). This means at `time == expires`, the other views already consider the item expired, but `expire()` does not remove it until `time > expires` (one tick later). This explains why `len()`/`currsize` still count the item and `expire()` returns empty at t=2, while `1 in cache` is False.

Fix: change the loop condition in `expire()` from `time > curr.expires` to `not (time < curr.expires)` (equivalently `time >= curr.expires`), matching the boundary used elsewhere, in `src/cachetools/__init__.py` inside `TTLCache.expire`.
